articleTitle: Informetric Analysis of Researches on Legal Issues Related to Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence technology has exerted a huge impact on all aspects of society including the legal field. Considerable research has been conducted on the legal issues related to artificial intelligence. Herein, taking 621 papers indexed by Thomson Reuters’s Web of Science as the object, the basic status of research on legal issues related to artificial intelligence was analyzed using the quantitative and visual analysis method. In terms of the research field, the results showed that the research on legal issues related to artificial intelligence shows interdisciplinary characteristics, that is, the legal issues related to artificial intelligence not only attract scholars in the legal field, but also those in computer science, engineering, social sciences, library and information science, business economics and other fields. In terms of keyword cooccurrence and cluster analysis, it was found that the legal issues related to artificial intelligence mentioned in these papers can be mainly divided into the following three categories: the first is the positive impact of artificial intelligence on practice of law, involving legal services, law enforcement, legal analysis (e.g., legal reasoning, legal argumentation), etc.; the second is the practical challenges possibly arising from artificial intelligence, including the determination of criminal responsibility, the governance of discrimination or bias risks, and the protection of copyright, privacy, and data rights; and the third is the regulatory solutions for artificial intelligence mainly focusing on ethical regulation, legislative regulation, technical regulation.

articleTitle: Research of Intelligent Recognition System for Teaching Links
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: As an important component of the teaching implementation process, teaching link is one of the important elements that teachers need to consider for effective teaching. At present, the recognition of teaching links based on teaching videos mainly adopts the manual method which has the defects of low efficiency and large time cost. In light of this, this paper investigates the intelligent recognition system for teaching links, which is designed and implemented from the teaching behavior characteristics with three functions to realize the rapid identification and positioning of teaching links. The classroom teaching video characteristic time period segmentation module divides different characteristic time periods from the teaching video; the teaching behavior sequence extraction module is used to obtain the teaching behavior sequence in each teaching link candidate segments; and the teaching link recognition module receives the final teaching link recognition results. This system can achieve the identification and localization of seven kinds of teaching links, which aims to provide technical support for teachers to engage in reflective professional development, as well as to provide a convenient platform for assisting teachers to carry out the intelligent identification of teaching links.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Applications and Roles in Supply Chain Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: This article investigates the intricate network of AI applications in the context of supply chain sustainability and the potential economic consequences that arise from it. Through an extensive examination of the available literature, the investigation delves into the theoretical dimensions of this developing area, constructs a conceptual model for comprehending the interconnectedness, and considers the mediating function of AI. The methodology mainly depends on a thorough examination of current literature to guide the creation of the framework. By synthesizing previous research, we clarify the interconnectedness of AI applications in driving sustainable practices in the supply chain and the subsequent impact on financial performance. This article is likely to establish a theoretical foundation and likely to act as a roadmap for future empirical research, providing an unstructured framework to examine the intricate relationships between AI, sustainability, and economic outcomes.

articleTitle: Split or Not to Predict Big Five Personality?
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Handwriting analysis for predicting personality traits can be used in different applications. However, most methods simply imitated graphologists’ operation, automatically extracted the features from graphologists’ recommendations, then fed the features into the classifiers to get the personality traits. In our paper, we provided a full-automatic approach to analyze the handwriting samples. We carried out a few experiments with a convolutional neural network structure for all the languages and only one language, with and without split, not considering the content of the samples. Experimental results showed that the split operation has a positive effect on test accuracy and loss, making up for the lack of training samples.

articleTitle: Application status and future prospect of SCADA industrial software in China
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: With the advent of the era of big data, big data has been applied to all walks of life to promote the digital development of China's industry. [Purpose/Significance] Based on the development status of industrial software in China, this paper deeply analyzes the application of SCADA software in China, and finally studies the analysis method of data collected by SCADA software. [Method/Process] In the process of writing this paper, this issue was summarized mainly according to the relevant literature research in CNKI. VOSviewer soft ware was used to extract keywords from the literature in CNKI, and finally presented in the form of a network graph. [Result/Conclusion] Through reading the relevant literature of CNKI, the research on the development of industrial software in China is concluded that industrial software in China has developed rapidly in recent years, but there is still a lack of research on R&D and design software. According to the literature of China National Knowledge Network, VOSviewer software was used to analyze the keywords in the literature, and the chart related to the correlation of keywords was obtained, which showed the application of SCADA software more clearly.

articleTitle: Data-driven Analysis of Children’s Digital Reading Behavior: System Design and Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Tracking, analyzing and guiding users' reading behavior based on big data indirectly is one of the key issues that need to be solved when digital reading moving towards intelligent reading. Currently, the digital reading platforms widely used for children have problems in monitoring the reading process and providing targeted feedback. Based on analysis of relevant research on digital reading behavior and children’s reading characteristics, this paper built a data model of digital reading behavior to collect and describe the data from multi-source and heterogeneous reading platforms. Then, the paper proposed an analytical framework for data of digital reading behavior, and visualized the analysis results from different dimensions and granularities. Finally, the paper developed the data analysis prototype system for digital reading behavior and took the data of more than 1,600 students, recorded in the practical application, as an example to carry out empirical research. This study can provide technical tools and methods for optimizing children’s digital reading platform.

articleTitle: GPTMORE: Generative Pre-trained Transformer for Model-based Offline Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Training sample collection in the real world or simulation environment is usually time-consuming and inefficient. Model-based offline reinforcement learning (RL) provides a feasible way to solve this problem by modeling the interaction environment of agents. However, the previous methods usually ignored the temporal correlation between different samples, resulting in a large deviation in the estimate of state transition, which decreases the learning efficiency and final performance. To address this issue, we proposed GPTMORE, the Generative Pretrained Transformer for Model-based Offline REinforcement learning. Based on the accurate estimation of the state transition dynamics from GPTMORE, we perform Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) for policy improvement. We instantiate GPTMORE in MuJoCo for robot control tasks and compare it with the state-of-the-art (SOTA) offline RL methods. The final performance of GPTMORE is better than the previous approaches in most tasks, which demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Opportunities and risks in the development of artificial intelligence and the Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: In the past 300 years, four industrial revolutions have taken place. From the rumbling steam trains to the high-speed trains that can reach 300 kilometers per hour, human science and technology have made a qualitative leap, this has also contributed to the well-being of human beings. The pursuit of spiritual life is driven by the increasing abundance of material life. This has indirectly led to the emergence of a virtual world called the "Metaverse" , which in conjunction with artificial intelligence, has developed in various ways, including augmented reality, the first year of the metasuniverse began. But everything has two sides, opportunity and risk are no exception, the rise of new things is not only a good opportunity to explore a better, ideal future, but also behind a certain risk. Therefore, the proper treatment and rational use of AI technology-related products is not irrelevant, it is about the future path of development.

articleTitle: Deep Convolution Neural Network in Clustering Explanation
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: This paper analyze the effectiveness of feature extraction of deep convolutional neural networks in image classification from the perspective of the basic statistical pattern recognition method, K-means clustering. This clustering works on those features extracted from each convolution layer of the VGG16 network, as well as the visualization of those features. The visualization graphs show the changes IOR of feature extraction from CNN, while the clustering graphs show the distribution of features extracted by CNN for different class samples. This work provides an interpretive perspective on the statistical learning methods of deep learning, and hope to provide values for readers.

articleTitle: Effects of Cognitive Biases on Performance of a VMI Program
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: This paper investigates how supply chain members acquire benefits in vendor-managed inventory (VMI) from a cognitive bias perspective. In a supply chain with a supplier and a retailer facing stochastic demand, the performance differences between the VMI and the retailer-managed inventory programs are analyzed and numerical experiments are conducted to investigate the effects of supply chain parameters. Conventional wisdom without considering rationality implies supplier's insufficient motivation to participate in VMI. However, both supply chain members can be actually better in VMI when paying attention to the match between their extent of rationality and the uncertain level of end demand.

articleTitle: Facial Micro-Expression Analysis: A Survey of Features and Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Unlike traditional facial expressions, micro-expressions are unconscious and brief facial expressions that true emotions people try to hide. Therefore, they can provide important information in a wide range of applications, including lie detection and criminal investigations. However, due to their brevity and low intensity, detecting and recognizing micro-expressions is challenging, and micro-expression analysis has become an active research field due to its inherent uniqueness and complexity in recent years. In this review paper, the research on micro-expression analysis is surveyed, including the neuropsychological basis, features, discovery algorithms, recognition algorithms, application and evaluation of state-of- the-art methods. For each aspect, the basic techniques, advanced developments, and key challenges are discussed and analyzed. Finally, some potential future research directions are explored and outlined.

articleTitle: A Novel Chess Interaction System Based on Visual Recognition and Generative Models: Virtual Gestures, Intelligent Assistant, and Multimodal Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: With the rapid development of computer vision algorithms and artificial intelligence generative models, interaction methods have become more diverse. This paper proposes a novel international chess interaction system that integrates virtual gesture recognition, large language model (LLM) intelligent assistant, and image-text generation technology to upgrade the traditional chess game experience in three aspects: interaction, decision-making, and feedback layers. We conducted a user survey on the prototype experience system and analyzed it in terms of intelligence and interactivity. In terms of interactivity, our user survey results showed that multimodal generation significantly improves interaction, while virtual interaction technology still needs optimization in usability. In terms of intelligence, the LLM intelligent assistant demonstrated certain usability and potential for higher win-rate improvement.

articleTitle: Deep Clustering and Dynamic Routing Based TSK Fuzzy System for Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) fuzzy system is a classical machine learning method with flexible modelling and good nonlinear approximation. However, as the data size and feature dimension increase, it has continually challenged the TSK fuzzy system to achieve satisfactory performance. Therefore, this paper proposes a TSK fuzzy system that combines deep clustering and the dynamic routing algorithm (DDTSK). Firstly, to accurately divide the complex input data space, a deep clustering based on sparse auto-encoder and K-means is proposed for determining the antecedent parameters. Then, a consequent parameters fine-tuning method based on dynamic routing is proposed to establish the correlation between input and output space. To further improve the classification performance, updating the output weights of the TSK fuzzy classifier via ridge regression algorithm. The experiments are conducted on 10 UCI machine learning datasets having different data sizes and feature dimensions. The experimental results show that the proposed optimization technique can further improve the accuracy and generalization of the TSK fuzzy system.

articleTitle: Real-time Interaction Force Modelling And Computing For Intracerebral Haemorrhage Preoperative Training Based On Rod-Particle Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: The onset of intracerebral haemorrhage is dangerous, and this condition changes very quickly. It is the primary cause of death and disability within the spectrum of senile diseases. Upon onset, the transfer time is very short, so patients need timely and effective remote treatments. At present, endoscopic craniotomy requires the collaboration of several surgeons and nurses, which leads to the problem of incomplete approaches. The existing surgical robots lack the ability to provide a 3D visualization of the surgical area and tactile sensation, resulting in inefficiency and secondary brain damage. To save patients in a timely and effective manner using-robot- assisted intracerebral haemorrhage preoperative training, there is an urgent need to study the interaction force modelling and calculation during the surgery to provide real-time visualization of the surgical process and to make up for the tactile loss during robotic surgery. In this paper, a rod-particle model is used to construct real-time interaction force modelling and computing between the endoport and the brain parenchyma. The particle swarm method is applied to optimize elastic coefficients according to experienced surgeons at Jinling Hospital. The interaction force is calculated and is fed back in realtime to the surgeons on the master side. Using left- and right-handed haptic robots and other equipment to build the visual intracerebral haemorrhage preoperative training experimental system, the real-time performance and accuracy of the proposed method are verified by experiments via the platform.

articleTitle: Maritime Radar Small Target Detection Based on Echo Embedding and Self-Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Radar small target detection is capable of effectively identifying small targets present on the sea surface. In recent years, deep learning methods have demonstrated strong performance in various fields, such as natural language processing and image analysis. This paper proposes a method for detecting small targets on the sea surface based on echo embedding and self-attention. Firstly, the radar time-frequency feature maps are embedded into high-dimensional space using patches to enhance the network of feature representation capabilities. Then, important features are extracted locally and globally through the feature self-attention module within specific windows. Finally, the detection of maritime small targets is achieved through a linear layer. Our method is validated based on the IPIX dataset. The experimental results indicate that our method achieved promising detection performance on the four subsets of the IPIX dataset.

articleTitle: Machine Learning and Covid-19 Data Predict Next Intercontinental Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Experiences from past Covid-19 pandemic have led to explore the actions that were taken previous time to the implementation of policies in a fast and optimal manner. Because of this actions the arrival of virus to a country would have to have exhibited a reduced number of infections and fatalities. Nevertheless it was not in that way as was observed in the global data, with a pandemic showing peaks of infections, waves and various virus mutations. This is the central focus of this paper: To understand the global data, so that one can employ this knowledge to identify as well as anticipate the possible apparition of a new virus. In this manner, this paper combines that Covid-19 global data and the criteria of Tom Mitchell to identify the levels of lethality of a new virus. To accomplish this, a cognitive algorithm is developed and it has as central purpose to find the matching between previous pandemic and new data of a pandemic in its first phase. As illustration, up to 6 countries were examined to assess their strengths again a new virus.

articleTitle: Effects of Object Complexity in Occlusion, Structure, and Texture on 3D Virtual Object Observation in Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) environments involve users in 3D virtual object interactions and manipulation tasks. Many of these are for the purpose of 3D virtual object observation, such as viewing a reconstructed museum artifact in a virtual museum. In this paper, we present a study that investigated the effects of object complexity in occlusion, structure, and texture on 3D virtual object observation in VR. We implemented a direct manipulation technique that allows users to grab, move, rotate, and scale an object for close-up observations. Twenty participants used the technique to manipulate virtual objects of various levels of complexity in occlusion, structure, and texture, to complete observation tasks (search and classify marks). The results showed that among the three dimensions of object complexity, occlusion and texture have significant impacts on users’ observation task completion time, but structure showed no significant impact. Our work contributes to the understanding of object complexity for 3D object observation in VR environments.

articleTitle: Human Versus Computer: Who Can Make Valuable Progress in Theoretical Physics?
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Nowadays, there is a solid consensus about the rapid progress of artificial intelligence and its potential usage in the different functions of society. This paper presents an example about contribution in theoretical physics done by human and computer. In concrete, attention is paid on the derivation of reduced Virasoro’s algebra. The derivation demands well- established steps that require expertise and a deeply knowledge of advanced mathematics. Thus, this paper exposes a competition between computer using machine learning (manifested at the criteria of Tom Mitchell) and humans, about the generation of reduced Virasoro’s algebra. In essence, it is explored the case where computer can provide smart procedures to generate algebra. It is seen that computers might be limited to manifest originalities as humans commonly do.

articleTitle: Conditional Probability For Identification of High Risk Event of Stroke
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: The beginning of stroke might be identified with a high confident, in particular in those cases where patients have an old diagnosis of type-II diabetes. More than an identification, the behavior of patient can be seen as a type of sequence to central event of stroke. In this paper, the variables that would lead to central event, are seen as conditions that enhance the central event. Therefore, it is postulated the idea that stroke is a probabilistic event caused by conditional probabilities. Because this argument, the full risk probability is estimated and a simulation is carry out. In this manner, stroke can be seen as a probability that is maximized by a weight function. Early recognition of this would be critic to clinicians in order to apply the best pharmacological strategy along the first minutes of stroke.

articleTitle: Analysis of Information Security Governance for Higher Education Institutions
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Information security problems in higher education institutions around the world are evident and frequent because there are no adequate models and prototypes based on the culture of education and a globalizing environment. The objective is to analyzed information security governance trends for a higher education institution. The deductive method and exploratory research were used for the analysis of documents and websites related to the research topic. The result of this investigation was Security algorithms using flowchart techniques, Conceptual model for governance, enterprise architecture applying information security governance, Simulations applying indicators and relevant actors for governance. It was concluded that in order to improve the governance of information security in higher education institutions, researchers continue to validate at least the ten relevant actors; In this research, ten simulations were carried out and the best result was obtained, 95% for the governance of information security through the simulations.

articleTitle: An Embedded System Design for Wildlife Detection and Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: When there is a need to monitor wildlife animals in the vast wilderness, power consumption is a challenging aspect in systems designed for such purposes. In this work, a low-power embedded-camera system for wildlife detection and identification is implemented. The design objectives of the system are to reduce the power consumption and system load of operation in an embedded environment through a prior movement detection strategy. An asynchronous multi-threaded concurrency mechanism is employed to increase the Frame Per Second (FPS). This system is beneficial for many applications in various wilderness areas, such as traffic alarms when large wild animals are crossing a highway, public warning systems of potential threats in urban areas indicating the presence of dangerous animals, and wildlife migrations monitoring by biologists.

articleTitle: Question Answering System based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, knowledge graph has been widely used in various fields. It can be used as a high-quality data source of question-answering system. A template-based method is used to implement the Aircraft knowledge graph question answering system. Firstly, entities in natural language problems are identified, and then classified. For problem understanding, three algorithms are proposed, which are Naive Bayesian and two algorithms based on distributed vector representation: doc2vec model and TextCNN model. Naive Bayesian algorithm, which first uses word-bag model to express questions and then classifies them. Doc2vec model converts questions into distributed sentence vectors and then the k-nearest neighbor algorithm is used to calculate the most similar template; TextCNN algorithm is used to train Word2vec model, and to train the network model of question comprehension. The experimental results show that the method based on TextCNN works best and achieves 94.2% accuracy on the manual labeled test set. This shows that the algorithm based on TextCNN can learn the semantic features of words and sentences well and understand the problem according to the semantic features. The method achieves good question-and-answer performance.

articleTitle: Security Algorithms and Protocols to Mitigate Data Risks in the Cloud in a Distributed Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Attacks on information security in the cloud have been manifested for many years, due to the types of services it offers, including data storage; Cloud attacks, security protocols, and benchmark algorithms were analyzed to identify security gaps that are vulnerable to different attacks. The main objective is to propose a Conceptual Model to protect the cloud against attacks. Qualitative, descriptive and deductive reasoning was used to analyze the information from the reference articles. It resulted in a Conceptual Model to protect the cloud against attacks, a Cloud Security Prototype and an Algorithm using flowchart techniques to protect the cloud from attacks. It was concluded that the conceptual model to protect the cloud from attacks proposed allows users to have an identity, authorization, authentication and audit (IAAA) so that the information has confidentiality, integrity and availability (CIA) in a distributed environment in the cloud.

articleTitle: An Ontology of Gradualist Machine Ethics
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Ethical gradualism is the idea that whether an entity possesses morality is not a yes-or-no question, but rather has answers on a gradual scale. Our paper contributes to the field of machine ethics by replacing the often used, and variously construed, concept of computer "morality" with the more specific concept of "moral relevance". This we define as "the characteristic of having some connection to the moral domain". Our definition requires that an entity's perceived moral relevance can be obtained as an aggregate of multi-axial, continuous-variable moral characteristics such as, but not limited to, patiency, responsibility, and autonomy. These characteristics can furthermore be broken down into concrete sub- (and sub-sub-, etc.) characteristics which are easier to measure in the real world. This gradualist model of perceived moral relevance can then be practically implemented through translation into Web Ontology Language. We depict moral relevance both graphically as a class hierarchy, and in computer code. Our implementation allows computers to recognize perceived moral relevance in other computers. This provides a basic architecture by which computers can learn perceived ethical behavior only by acting with one another. The implementation also makes possible a new kind of experimental moral psychology, in which researchers can compare gradual perceived moral relevance directly between humans and computers.

articleTitle: Effects of Virtual Reality on Mechanical Arm Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: In this study, we aimed to explore the effects of virtual reality (VR) on the skill learning process and outcome of mechanical arms. We adopted the unequal groups for the experiment, and analyzed the process and outcome of skill learning based on behavior sequences. We invited 56 students from a university of science and technology as the participants to study the learning of mechanical arm technology. The main conclusions are as follows: 1) According to the evaluation results of skill learning, VR had a highly positive effect on skill learning from seven aspects, including perception, set, guided response, mechanism, complex overt response, adaptation, and origination; the results of the experimental group were superior to those of the control group. 2) During the learning of VR operations, the behavioral transfer from the autonomous phase to the autonomous phase was the most significant, followed by that from the correction phase to the fixation phase.

articleTitle: Enhancing Emotional Engagement in Virtual Reality (VR) Cinematic Experiences through multi-sensory Interaction Design
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: This research paper explores the potential of multisensory interaction design to enhance emotional engagement in virtual reality (VR) cinematic experiences. With VR technology becoming increasingly prevalent, there is a growing interest in creating immersive narratives that evoke powerful emotional responses. The challenge lies in effectively leveraging the multisensory capabilities of VR to deepen emotional engagement. This paper proposes a framework that combines theoretical foundations from emotional psychology, human-computer interaction, and sensory design to guide the development of multi-sensory interactions in VR cinematic experiences. This research aims to provide insights into the design principles, techniques, and considerations for creating emotionally impactful VR cinematic experiences through a comprehensive review of existing literature and case studies.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection for Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) is an important stage between Normal Control (NC) and Alzheimer's disease (AD), thus the early detection of MCI carries important clinical significance. Anomaly detection can identify abnormal regions in medical images and serve as a tool for early diagnosis and treatment of MCI patients. However, the absence of pixel-level labels in the MCI database poses a challenge to performing anomaly detection using supervised learning. Unsupervised learning can be utilized as an alternative approach to address the above-mentioned issues. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised anomaly detection framework based on the diffusion model for the early detection of MCI. The proposed framework learns the distribution of healthy data and guides the abnormal data to conform to the healthy distribution, thereby achieving "healing" and locating anomaly regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework can effectively distinguish between healthy and abnormal data, and highlight anomaly regions associated with MCI, showing its practical significance in the early diagnosis of MCI.

articleTitle: A Review on AI-based Modeling of Empathetic Conversational Response Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Empathy is a complex psychological concept consisting of affective and cognitive aspects. It plays a crucial role in human communication. Dialogue systems are designed to interact with people in natural language. Integrating empathy into dialogue systems is valuable to enhance user experience, although it is a challenging task. Existing studies in Empathetic Conversational Response Generation (ECRG) have made notable advancements. However, their focus has mainly been on specific facets of empathy, such as mimicking the user’s emotions and integrating commonsense knowledge to enhance cognitive empathy. This leaves opportunities for further exploration in areas such as enhancing self-other awareness. This paper will conduct a comprehensive review of empathy theories to bridge this gap, offering a theoretical understanding of empathy in various dimensions. Additionally, it critically reviews existing studies on ECRG, including algorithms, methods to address affective empathy and cognitive empathy, datasets, and evaluation methods. By highlighting the technical challenges and opportunities, this review provides guidance for researchers on AI research for modeling empathy in dialogue systems by investigating empathetic response generation for conversational AI modeling.

articleTitle: A Survey of an Evaluation Index of Teaching Ability for Financial Literacy Education Based on TPACK for Primary and Secondary School Teachers
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: Based on the TPACK theoretical framework, this study used the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) to construct an evaluation index system to explore the current situation of the teaching ability of financial literacy education of primary and secondary school teachers in Guangxi through the opinions of 10 experts. The results of AHP were consistent, and the importance of composite factor indicators (TPACK, TPK, TCK, PCK) was higher than that of core factor indicators (PK, TK, CK). The results of reliability and validity tests showed that the scale has good reliability and validity. A total of 1,022 primary and secondary school teachers in Guangxi were randomly selected for investigation. The results showed that the average of male teachers was higher than that of female teachers for the dimensions of CK, PK, TK, PCK, TCK and TPK; the average of urban teachers in seven dimensions was higher than that of county teachers; the teachers with less teaching experience performed better than those with more than 10 years of teaching experience; the performance of primary school teachers was better than that of junior high school teachers; and the better the school ICT teaching equipment, the better the teachers' performance on the indicators. The results of this study can provide a good reference for future empirical research.

articleTitle: Embodied Cognition Guides Virtual-Real Interaction Design to Help Yicheng Flower Drum Intangible Cultural Heritage Dissemination
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: In order to make the non-heritage culture of Yicheng Flower Drum more relevant to the trend of the digital era and promote its dissemination and inheritance, the design and application of gesture recognition and virtual reality technologies guided by embodied cognition theory in the process of non-heritage culture dissemination is studied. At the same time, it will enhance the interaction between people and NRM culture, stimulate the audience’s interest in understanding NRM and spreading NRM, and create awareness of preserving NRM culture. Using embodied cognition as a theoretical guide, expanding the unidirectional communication mode through human-computer interaction close to natural behavior and cooperating with multisensory information reception channels, so as to construct an embodied and immersive interactive atmosphere for the participants and enable them to naturally form the cognition and understanding of the traditional culture in the process of interaction. The dissemination of the non-heritage culture Yicheng Flower Drum can take the theory of embodied cognition as an entry point, and through the virtual and real scenes of Yicheng Flower Drum and the immersive experience, we can empower the interaction design of non-heritage culture dissemination of the virtual and real, and provide a new method for the research of digital design of non-heritage culture.

articleTitle: Quantitative determination of heavy metals by CARS assisted extreme learning machine using x-ray fluorescence
publicationTitle: 2023 Asia Conference on Cognitive Engineering and Intelligent Interaction (CEII)
abstract: To reduce environmental pollution, it is crucial to conduct research on efficient, inexpensive, and accurate ways to measure the concentration of heavy metals. However, currently used x-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometers are inaccurate in measuring the low concentration of heavy metals. To address the aforementioned issues, a new prediction framework was proposed and implemented in MATLAB, including denoising, background deduction, feature selection, and decision-making. First, the wavelet hard threshold denoising (WHTD) method and the iterative discrete wavelet transform (IDWT) method were applied to denoise and correct the baseline of spectrums, respectively. Then, a heavy metal estimation model based on competitive adaptive reweighted sampling assisted extreme learning machine (CARS-ELM) was proposed. In detail, the CARS algorithm was utilized to select characteristic spectral lines for the target element, and a non-linear relationship between the selected lines and element concentration was established using the ELM method. The results showed that the CARS-ELM model predicted the concentration of Cr, Cu, Zn, As, Cd, and Pb accurately, with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values of 0.991, 0.999, 0.999, 0.994, 0.993, and 0.995, respectively. It is demonstrated that heavy metal concentration can be accurately predicted using the XRF technique in conjunction with the proposed framework.
